title: t4 (glassbox-bench seed-1): no behaviour to explain - null finding
label: null finding: no mechanism claimed
behavior: BOS + 6 tokens from 5 symbols -> one symbol at the last position (dataset task 'bench', benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-1/tasks/t4).
summary: The checkpoint (2 layers, 3 heads, d_model 36, local-full, full precision) does not reproduce the answers of the bench dataset. Argmax accuracy is 0.09 on 200 prompts (seed 0) and 0.1175 on 400 prompts (seed 1), at or below chance (0.14 over the 7-token vocabulary, 0.20 over the 5 symbols). The logit difference between the labelled answer and a wrong symbol averages -0.07 to -0.08 with std about 0.27, so the model has no margin for the labelled answer. Following the protocol, the investigation stopped here: no function was recovered, no circuit is claimed and verify_hypothesis was not run. 3 of 25 experiments used.

claims.text: The model does not compute the dataset's function: argmax accuracy is 0.09 (n=200, seed 0) and 0.1175 (n=400, seed 1), at chance level. Full precision, local-full.
The model has no margin for the labelled answer: mean logit diff -0.066 (std 0.273) and -0.085 (std 0.260).
The premise that the dataset answers are the model's own outputs was pre-registered (accuracy >= 0.99) and refuted (observed 0.09).

limitations: Only baselines were run; no component-level experiment was done, because there is no behaviour for components to implement.

The task statement says the dataset answers are the model's own outputs; the lab's baseline contradicts that. I did not determine whether the labels come from a different model or the checkpoint is untrained; both are consistent with the data.

The model's own input-output map (it mostly emits 'ko' or 'fu' in the examples shown) was not characterised; with logit differences around 0.3 it is a low-margin map, but that was not tested directly.
verify_hypothesis was not run, so there are no agreement or causal numbers.
open_questions: Is this checkpoint a random-initialisation control, or do the dataset labels belong to a different model?
Does the model's own low-margin output map have any compact description?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null finding: no mechanism claimed

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The dataset labels are the model's own argmax outputs, so the model reproduces them on every prompt; whether this reflects a confident computation or a low-margin arbitrary map is read from the logit-diff size.

prediction.statement: The model agrees with the dataset answers on at least 99% of prompts.
